## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Jarasiṅgālaṅgapañha* ("The Old Male Jackal", Mil 7.5.6) is a discourse found within the seventh book of the *Milindapañha* [SuttaCentral]. In this section of the work, various natural traits and behaviors of animals or objects are allegorized as virtuous qualities (*aṅga*) to be emulated by the Buddhist practitioner. SuttaCentral notes a connection between this discourse and the verses of Mahākassapa in the *Theragāthā* (*Mahākassapattheragāthā*, Thag 18.1) [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral indexes three modern translations across three languages for this text [SuttaCentral].

No curated canonical parallels in other languages are cataloged by SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral]. However, text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus identifies extensive formulaic parallels internal to the Pali canon, recording 200 matching passages across 44 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. These matches consist almost entirely of shared framing and repetitive rhetorical formulas common across the simile-based inquiries of the seventh book of the *Milindapañha*, such as the *Kummaṅgapañha* (Mil 7.2.6), *Meghaṅgapañha* (Mil 7.7.6), *Sīhaṅgapañha* (Mil 7.6.1), and *Issāsaṅgapañha* (Mil 7.8.7) [DharmaNexus]. Across languages, DharmaNexus automatically aligns the text with five passages in the Tibetan translation of the Mahāyāna *Ratnarāśisūtra* (*Ārya-ratnarāśi-nāma-mahāyānasūtra*, D0088), including an alignment between Mil 7.5.6 §4.1–4.3 and folio 170a, though with a low plausibility score of 25 [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
